manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Hang the cup on the rack.

Task description: Pick up the white handled cup on the left side of the table and hang it by its handle on the projecting bar of the wooden rack to its right.

Success criteria: The cup has been picked up, the hanging bar passes through the cup handle hole and supports it, and the cup body is suspended above the table on the rack; merely leaning the cup against the rack does not count as completion.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping a cup-mouth wall section away from the handle, with one finger inside and one outside and pads below the rim. Adjust the opening for wall thickness and surrounding clearance, leaving room to thread the handle onto the rod.
- Before closing, use both views to confirm the inner finger has entered the cup opening and both fingers enclose the same section of the wall. Avoid pressing on the rim or relying on image overlap with the wall.
- When turning the cup handle toward the rack bar, make small pose adjustments while the cup base is off the table and the body is away from the stand. Leave room for the gripper and handle to rotate, reducing the risk of brushing the table or bar.
- Choose a hanging rod with ample surrounding clearance, face the cup-handle opening toward its tip, and slide it on in small steps along the rod. Watch spacing from the cup body to the post and adjacent rods, avoiding contact between the rod tip and the cup wall or outer handle edge.
- Before releasing, let the handle settle gently on the rod and confirm the rod bears the load, then slowly relax the gripper to avoid slipping when the handle rests only on the tip. Withdraw clear of the cup mouth and handle to reduce pulling the cup or stand.
